full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J. This Jail Appeal preferred by the condemned appellants 1. Md. Shahin Alam Shahin and 2. Md. Mizanur Rahman Mizan against the judgment and order dated 08.07.2012 passed by the High Court Division in Death Reference No.21 of 2008 heard analogously with Criminal Appeal Nos.1294, 1297 and 1309 of 2008 with Jail Appeal Nos.288-290 of 2008 accepting the death reference and dismissing the appeals thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 28.02.2008 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Patuakhali in Sessions Case No.50 of 2007 arising out of Kalapara Police Station Case No.17 dated 31.01.2007, corresponding to G.R. No.17 of 2007 convicting the appellants under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing them to death. 

 2. The prosecution case, as it revealed from the evidence of P.W. 1 Raihan Gofur is that the unfortunate victim Tahmina Sharmin alias Tania was a brilliant student who secured First Division in S.C.C. and H.S.C. and obtained First Class in M.A. She was given in marriage with convict Zahid Hossain Jewel. She gave birth to a son named Zaimon who was 10 months old at the time of occurrence. On 27.01.2007, the convict Zahid Hossain Jewel, taking the victim Tania and son Zaimon, went to Kuakata from Dhaka by his private car and stayed in a Porjatan Corporation hotel named "Holiday Homes" from 27.01.2007 to 30.01.2007. At about 7 p.m. on 30.01.2007, they left Kuakata for Dhaka and at about 11/11.30 p.m. reaching near village Rojapara under Kalapara Police Station the appellants and Zahid assaulting the victim with sharp cut-ting weapons, mercilessly killed her. One Abdul Mannan informed the matter to Kalapara Police Station. The police rushed to P.O. and recovered Tania and shifted her to Kalapara Thana Health Complex where the doctor on duty declared her dead. Kalapara Police informed the matter to the father of the victim Tania. Being informed P. W.1. rushed to the Health Complex, Kalapara and identified the victim. The appellants fled away towards Patuakhali taking Zahid's car which was recovered from a place called Hetalia. At about 8/8.30 p.m. on 31.01.2007, P.W.1 lodged First Information Report with Kalapara Police Station. 

 4. The case was ultimately tried by the Sessions Judge Patuakhali who framed charges against the appellants and Zahid under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. The accused, on dock, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The prosecution examined 30 witnesses in support of its case and defence examined none. From the trend of cross examination of the prosecution witnesses it appears that the defence case was of innocence and that some unknown miscreants attacked the car of the husband of the victim Tania in order to commit dacoity and they stabbed Zahid and Tania. Subsequently, Tania died. 

 5. The trial Court, examining the accused on dock under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record, convicted Zahid Hossain Jewel and appellants Md. Shahin Alam Shahin and Md. Mizanur Rahman Mizan under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced each of them to death. The Sessions Judge transmitted the case record to the High Court Division for confirmation of the sentence of death. The appellants and the husband of the victim, namely, Zahid preferred appeals and jail appeals in the High Court Division against the judgment and order of the learned Sessions Judge. 

 7. In order to prove the case the prosecution examined 30 witnesses. Out of those witnesses P.W.1, brother of the victim Tania, is the informant of the ease who narrated the prosecution case in his testimony. He said, Tania was a genius girl who secured glorious result in every academic examination and that she gave birth to a child, namely, Zaimon Zahid. The marital life of her sister was not so happy. Tahmina Sharmin Tania, Zaimon Zahid and Zahid Hossain went to Kuakata for a pleasure trip at sea beach on 27.01.2007 by their private car and stayed in room no.201, of Holiday Homes, Parjatan Motel. On the way of returning, at about 11.00/11.30 p.m. when they reached at village Rajapara the accused persons with intent to kill Tania, inflicted stab injuries on her person. One Abdul Mannan informed the matter to Kalapara Police Station and the police, getting such information, rushed to the spot and shifted the victim to local hospital where the doctor declared her dead. Kalapara Police informed the matter to the informant party, accordingly, they rushed to the Kalapara health complex and identified the stab injured dead body of the deceased and, thereafter, lodged F.I.R. He came to know the fact of killing of his sister by the convict Zahid Hossain Jewel with the help of appellants Md. Shahin Alam Shahin and Md. Mizanur Rahman Mizan from the confessional statements made by them admitting their guilt. In course of Cross-examination the P.W.1 denied that his maternal uncle Habibur Rahman wrote the F.I.R on 30.10.2007. He added that he was not aware whether the husband of the victim convict Zahid deposited Tk.10 lacs in FDR account nominating the victim and her son as nominees and purchased ornaments of Tk.4 lac for Tania after their marriage. Be admitted that earlier the convict Zahid and the victim went to Cox's Bazar and Jaflong for pleasure trips. He denied that he brought the facts of marital disputes between Zahid and victim for the purpose of strengthening the prosecution case. He denied the defence suggestion that he influenced the police for bringing false case against the accused persons. 

 14. P.W.9 Khuki Begum in her testimony stated that on 17 Magh of the last year, at about 11.00-11.30 p.m. her sister, Chacha, Fufu and she went to the highway hearing a hue and cry. They found a red coloured private car plying away from the spot towards Patuakhali. She rushed to the spot and found a dead body lying on the western side of the road and husband of the deceased told that miscreants had killed the victim. Police rushed to the spot on receiving information and shifted the victim to Kalapara health complex. She took care of the baby of the victim throughout the night. She identified Zahid on dock. She stated that police seized a razor, blood stained knife and earth from the place of occurrence in her presence and she put her signature in the seizure list (Ext.3). 

 15. P.W.10 Fatima Begum in her testimony stated that while she was staying at her home at about 11.00/11.30 p.m., she heard a sound of screaming from highway and rushed there along with others and found a dead body of a woman lying on the western side of the road and saw that a red coloured private car going towards Patuakhali from the spot. She stated that the husband of the victim disclosed that the miscreants had killed his wife. A motorcycle rider informed the police about the incident who rushed to the spot within few minutes and shifted injured person and the victim to the hospital. This witness indentified the accused Zahid Hossain Jewel on dock. She denied that she deposed falsely being influenced by the prosecution. 

 25. P.W.29 Abdul Khaleque was then O.C. Kalapara who recorded the F.I.R. being presented the same before him at about 20.30 p.m. on 31.01.2007 by informant Raihan Gafur. He filled up the blank columns of the F.I.R. form and entrusted S.I. Farooquzaman as I.O. of the case. In cross-examination he denied that the date of lodging of the G.D. was erased and another date was interpolated. 

 26. P.W.30 Farooquzzaman was the Investigating Officer of the case who stated that he was S.I. attached to Kalapara P.S. He started investigation on the basis of a C.D. bearing No.l 003, dated 30.01.2007 lodged by one Abdul Mannan Sharif who informed that a woman was killed at Rajapara village. They rushed to the spot on the basis of such information and shifted the victim to the local health complex for treatment and that he seized incriminating articles and prepared seizure list. He prepared sketch map and its index. He went to Hetalia village being informed over telephone that a private car had been left abandoned there and seized the same along with the wearing apparels and other belongings of the deceased. He prepared a seizure list. He said that he took some photographs from the spot. He deposed that he recorded the statements of the witnesses and arrested the accused Zahid Hossain Jewel and took him on remand. During investigation, Zahid decided to make confession and accordingly, he forwarded Zahid before the Magistrate who recorded his confessional statement. He took step to arrest appellants Mizanur Rahman Mizan and Shahin Alam Shahin. He forwarded the appellants before the magistrate who recorded their confessional statements. He added that as per admission of the appellant Mizanur Rahman he had seized camera and one cell phone sup-plied by Nasima, wife of Mizan. He went to Hotel Zonaki on the basis of information given by the appellant Mizan and seized certain documents and also went to Kuakata and collected materials from the Hotel Holiday Homes. He collected evidence from the Hotel Shamudra Bilash as well. He submitted the charge sheet against three accused persons for committing oftence punishable under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code. In cross-examination, he stated that he recorded the statements of witnesses Aziz, Khooki Begum, Tafima, Renu Begum, Abdul Jabber and Nur Mohammad as per provi-sions of section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and seized some incriminating articles before lodging F.I.R on the basis of the G.D. He forwarded the accused Zahid Hossain before the court on 01.02.2007 who was in police custody before such forwarding. He denied the defence suggestion that he tortured the accused persons inhumanly and put them in fear of crossfire in order to secure their confessional statements which were not voluntary and true, that he did not produce accused Shahin Alam and Mizanur Rahman to the nearest Magistrate after ensuring their arrest. He denied the suggestion that he did not perform the investigation properly and the same was perfunctory and that the accused Zahid and his family was attacked and injured by a gang of miscreants whereby Tania succumbed to death and that he performed the investigation being influenced by the maker of the F.I.R. and his father. 

 31. Mr. Helaluddin Mollah, learned Advcoate engaged by the State appearing on behalf of the appellant Md. Shahin Alam Shahin submits that there is no eye witnesses of the occurrence and that the appellant has been convicted on the basis of confessional statement which was not voluntarily made and contents of the same were not truc and that was not recorded following the provisions of section 164 and 364 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further submits that the rosecution has failed to prove its case beyond all shadow of doubt by examining any eyewitness of the occurrence. 

 35. The doctor opined that the death was caused due to shock and hemorrhage resulting from those injuries which was anti-mortem and homicidal in nature. Dr. Nur Hossain, who held autopsy of the dead body of the victim was examined as P.W.2, proved the post-mortem report (Exhibit-2). From the said report and evidence of P.W.2 it is proved that the victim was mercilessly killed by inflicting as many as 8 stabbed injuries on her person. We do not find any elements in the post mortem report that contradicts confessional statements of the appellant Md. Shahin Alam or the other convicts, namely, Zahid and Mizan. Confessional statements of the three convicts including the appellant which were recorded on three different dates testify veracity of one another. Therefore, we have no doubt that those were true. P.W.19 A.K.M. Mamunur Rashid proved the confessional statements. He endorsed that the confessional statements were made voluntarily. In his evidence, he said that complying all legal formalities he recorded the confessional statements of the appellant and other convicts. On careful consideration of confessional statements and companng them with rest of the evidence in light of the surrounding circumstances and probabilities of the case, we are of the view, that findings of the courts below as to true nature and voluntary character of the confessions are correct. From the confessional statement of the appellant Md. Shahin Alam Shahin and oral and circumstantial evidence revealed from the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses, we have no hesitation to hold that the prosecution has been able to prove the charge against the appellant Md. Shahin Alam Shahin beyond all shadows of doubt. 

 37. The legislature has left the discretion to the court to award the appropriate punishment, in a case of murder. It is impossible to lay down any specific standard for awarding a particular sentence in any given case. This has to be determined according to the facts and circumstances of the case. The measure of punishment depends upon the brutality of the crime and the conduct of the offender. The Courts should impose sentence befitting the offence keeping in view not only the rights of offender, but also the rights of the victim of the crime. In the instant case appellant Md. Shahin Alam Shahin in collusion with convict Zahid hatched conspiracy to murder the victim Tania and contacted convict Mizan for executing the plan. He received taka 10,000/- for this purpose from convict Zahid. As per plan he drove the car of Zahid taking him, victim Tania and her infant son Zaimon in it to Kuakata. Reaching Kuakata appellant Shahin stayed in hotel Somudra Bilash. He met with convict Mizan and finalized plan to murder Tania with a razor and a knife. As per the plot he started driving car on 30.01.07 in the evening and at about 11/11.30 p.m. stopped the car at the place of occurrence upon receiving signal from convict Mizan. Getting out of the car he pretended to examine it by opening its bonnet for its sudden malfunctioning and thereby facilitated attack upon victim Tania by convict Mizan. After making sure that the victim had succumbed to her stab injuries, appellant Shahin made 4/5 shallow cut injuries in the body of the convict Zahid to cover up the murder showing it to be an incident of mugging resulted in killing of victim Tania and bodily injury of convict Zahid. This is a well-planned, cold blooded and cruel murder carried out in a dastardly manner. There is no evidence that the appellant committed the gruesome murder in response to a provocation or instigation made by the victim. Rather, he has admitted in his confession that he agreed to commit the murder in exchange of money. It seems that the idea of putting an end to a precious life for some material considerations is not disturbing to this appellant. He does not feel the sting of conscience for the offence he has committed. Such offender poses real threat to the society. We do not find any mitigating circumstance to warrant punishment lesser than death for such offender who can be hired for killing innocent people. Rented killers should not be shown any mercy defying the cry of the society for justice.
